Looking at this position, let me analyze the tactical opportunity.

**Position Analysis:**
- Black's king on c8 is somewhat exposed with rooks on d8 and e8
- Black's queen on c4 is actively placed but undefended
- White's knight on e4 is centralized and active

**The Solution:**

The clearly best move is **Nd6+**. This delivers check to the king on c8 while simultaneously attacking the undefended queen on c4—a classic royal fork.

After Nd6+:
- If Kd7, Nxc4 wins the queen
- If Kb8/Kb7/Kc7, Nxc4 still wins the queen
- Black has no way to save the queen

This wins material decisively.

**Coaching Note:**
When an enemy king and queen are on the same diagonal or knight-move distance, check if your knight can fork them. Nd6+ forces the king to move while attacking the queen—a fundamental pattern worth ingraining into your tactical vision. Always scan centralized knights for these opportunities.
